items.title: The normalization of the base in a disjoint union is the disjoint union of the normalizations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the normalization of the base in a disjoint union of two schemes is the disjoint union of the normalizations in the two pieces (statement lines 14312-14318). The counted proof reduces the geometric statement to the algebraic statement about the integral closure of a ring in a product of rings, and then gives the key reason why the statement holds, namely that the standard idempotents of the product are integral over the base ring and hence belong to the integral closure, which forces it to be a product whose factors are the individual integral closures (proof lines 14320-14330). It is H2: the reduction and the decisive observation are in the counted span; the author explicitly leaves 'some details' to the reader at the end, and what is left there is the routine identification of the two factors, not the mechanism of the proof.
